title: Jonah and the Protocol
premise: Quentin Thornbury maintains the Meridian Beacon, a deep-space relay whose original purpose has been lost to bureaucratic decay, when it intercepts a distress call in Ashkari — a language extinct since the Purge Fleets burned its homeworld two centuries ago. Decoding it, she discovers the beacon was built to broadcast a fabricated ceasefire between the descendants of those fleets, a lie sustained by automated transmissions no living person verifies. When both fleets converge on the beacon to finally learn the truth of their ancestors' war, Quentin must impersonate the protocol's dead architects in real time, weaving new lies from a dead tongue to keep them apart. In the end she chooses to broadcast the truth instead — and discovers the Ashkari signal was never a distress call at all, but an invitation to remember.
about_author: Gideon Nystrom is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years maintaining automated lighthouse beacons along a shrinking coastline. Their fiction explores what machines remember after people forget, and has appeared in several small-press anthologies of quiet science fiction.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. On the decaying Meridian station, Quentin catalogs her fading ability to dream in human languages while performing ritual maintenance on a beacon no one can explain. The emotional beat is loneliness sharpened into unease: she realizes her logs show transmissions she never authored, arriving on schedule for decades.

chapters.title: Ashkari Rising
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A distress signal arrives in extinct Ashkari; Quentin, one of three living scholars of the language, decodes fragments suggesting survivors exist aboard a drifting hulk. Excitement curdles into dread as she cross-references fleet records and finds the beacon's commissioning order signed by someone who died before construction began.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Lie
chapters.summary: POV alternating Quentin and Vess Okonjo, a Concord fleet intelligence officer ordered to investigate the beacon. Both discover the beacon broadcasts a fabricated ceasefire to two armadas poised on old grudges. The beat is vertigo: the peace holding two fleets apart may rest entirely on this forgotten machine.

chapters.title: What the Machine Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Deep in the beacon's archives she finds the architects' final entries — they knew the lie would fail eventually and left instructions in Ashkari for whoever came next. She begins learning the protocol's voice. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into resolve, as she mourns strangers across two centuries.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV Vess. Vess arrives at Meridian under orders to seize or destroy the beacon before either fleet learns the truth. She and Quentin circle each other through tense negotiations; Vess conceals that her own family history is entangled with the Purge Fleets. Beat: wary mutual recognition between two keepers of secrets.

chapters.title: The Convergence
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Both fleets alter course toward the beacon after a third party leaks its existence. Quentin begins broadcasting improvised transmissions in the architects' style, buying days with invented diplomatic communiqués. Beat: exhilaration and terror fused — she is fluent now in a language made entirely of lies.

chapters.title: Fracture Point
chapters.summary: POV Vess. Vess's superiors order her to kill the beacon and let the fleets settle it; refusing means treason. She confronts Quentin, who confesses everything including the distress signal's true content. Beat: betrayal and trust colliding — Vess must decide whether the truth is worth a war stopped only by a lie.

chapters.title: Dead Tongue, Living Voice
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The ruse collapses when a fleet commander demands direct contact with the 'architects.' Quentin answers live, speaking Ashkari over open channels, channeling two centuries of the dead. Climax builds: her performance holds the fleets motionless, but the strain fractures her already-dreamless mind.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV alternating Quentin and Vess. Cornered by verification teams from both fleets, Quentin abandons the lie and broadcasts the full archive: the war's real cause, the genocide, the architects' confession, and the Ashkari signal itself. Beat: cathartic exposure — every hidden thing laid bare at once, fleets frozen mid-approach.

chapters.title: An Invitation to Remember
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The fleets stand down, not from the lie but from shame; the surviving Ashkari hulk answers, revealing the signal was a summons to witness, not a plea for rescue. Quentin dreams that night — in Ashkari. Final beat: justice outside the law begins with memory, and memory needs keepers.
